candidates.label: Jahiliyyah thought: pre-Islamic fatalistic assumptions resurfacing in believers under battlefield crisis
candidates.definition: In 3:154: Then there came upon you after the distress security — drowsiness covering a party of you, while another party had become anxious about themselves, thinking wrongly about Allah with the assumption of jahiliyyah.

evidence.excerpt: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةٗ نُّعَاسٗا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةٗ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةٞ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءٖۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءٞ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
evidence.rationale: Zann al-jahiliyyah explicitly named as the cognitive framework of the anxious party. Contrasts with divine assurance (amanatan nu'asan) given to the other party.

candidates.urduLabel: جاہلیانہ سوچ: بحران میں پرانی عقیدہ
candidates.notes: Gap candidate: no dedicated jahiliyyah-thought or pre-islamic-mindset topic. Unique explicit naming of jahiliyyah cognition within a believer context. Shows how crisis triggers regression to pre-faith assumptions.

candidates.label: Divine pardon after failure: Allah's 'afw toward believers despite battlefield disobedience and weakness
candidates.definition: In 3:152: Until when you lost courage and fell to disputing about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you back from them in order to test you. And He has already pardoned you. And Allah is the Possessor of Bounty for the believers.

evidence.excerpt: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
evidence.rationale: Wa laqad 'afa 'ankum follows triple failure diagnosis (fashil/tanazu'/asa). Pardon precedes any repentance mention, emphasizing divine initiative. Dhu fadl frames pardon as bounty not obligation.

candidates.urduLabel: ناکامی کے بعد عفو: اللہ کا عفو
candidates.notes: Overlap with divine-mercy and repentance confirmed. Distinctive as pardon granted BEFORE explicit repentance. Context is collective military failure, not individual sin. 'Afw differs from maghfirah in scope.

candidates.label: Counterfactual grief prohibition: divine making of hasrah (regret) in hearts through 'what if' thinking about the dead
candidates.definition: In 3:156: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers who traveled through the land or were fighting, 'If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed,' so that Allah makes that a source of regret in their hearts.

evidence.excerpt: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقَالُواْ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَوۡ كَانُواْ غُزّٗى لَّوۡ كَانُواْ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ وَمَا قُتِلُواْ لِيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ حَسۡرَةٗ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٞ
evidence.rationale: La takoonoo ka-allatheena kafaroo establishes behavioral boundary. Li-yaj'ala Allahu dhalika hasratan fi quloobihim reveals divine pedagogical purpose of allowing regret.

candidates.urduLabel: فرضی غم کی ممنوعیت: حسرت کا بنانا
candidates.notes: Overlap with sabr-patience confirmed. Unique psychological insight: counterfactual thinking ('if only') identified as kafir-pattern behavior. Hasrah as divine-made consequence rather than natural emotion. Connects to qadar theology.

candidates.label: Scripture commodification: selling divine revelation for trivial worldly gain as wretched purchase
candidates.definition: In 3:187: And when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, 'You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it.' But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.

evidence.excerpt: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُۥ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكۡتُمُونَهُۥ فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَآءَ ظُهُورِهِمۡ وَٱشۡتَرَوۡاْ بِهِۦ ثَمَنٗا قَلِيلٗاۖ فَبِئۡسَ مَا يَشۡتَرُونَ
evidence.rationale: Ishtaraw bihi thamanan qaleelan: explicit commercial metaphor for scripture betrayal. Bi'sa ma yashtaroon evaluates the transaction as wretched.

candidates.urduLabel: کتاب کی تجارت: ممولی منافع کے لیے وحی بیچنا
candidates.notes: Gap candidate: no dedicated scripture-commodification or religious-corruption-for-gain topic. Commercial vocabulary (ishtara/thaman/qaleel) frames spiritual betrayal as economic transaction. Echoes 2:79 (wail li-allatheena yaktuboona).

candidates.label: Mata' al-ghurur: worldly life definitively characterized as enjoyment of delusion
candidates.definition: In 3:185: And what is the worldly life except the enjoyment of delusion.

evidence.excerpt: كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
evidence.rationale: Wa ma al-hayat al-dunya illa mata' al-ghurur: definitive equation using illa (nothing except). Ghurur implies active deception, not mere transience.

candidates.notes: Overlap with day-of-judgment via eschatological framing. Distinctive vocabulary: mata' (temporary provision/enjoyment) + ghurur (delusion/deception). Stronger than mere 'transient' characterization. Appears twice in this passage range (3:171, 3:185).

candidates.label: Hypocrite proximity to kufr: verbal profession of faith disconnected from heart conviction as closer to disbelief
candidates.definition: In 3:167: They are the ones who said about their brothers while they sat at home, 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.' Say, 'Then prevent death from yourselves, if you should be truthful.' They were closer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts.

evidence.excerpt: وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْۚ وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ قَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوِ ٱدۡفَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ لَوۡ نَعۡلَمُ قِتَالٗا لَّٱتَّبَعۡنَٰكُمۡۗ هُمۡ لِلۡكُفۡرِ يَوۡمَئِذٍ أَقۡرَبُ مِنۡهُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ يَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَٰهِهِم مَّا لَيۡسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَكۡتُمُونَ
evidence.rationale: Hum li-al-kufr yawma-idhin aqrabu minhum li-al-iman: explicit proximity measurement. Yaquoloona bi-afwahihim ma laysa fi quloobihim defines the disconnect.

candidates.urduLabel: منافقین کا کفر سے قرب: زبانی اقرار بغیر دلی یقین
candidates.notes: Gap candidate: no dedicated hypocrisy-psychology or nifaq-inner-state topic. Distinctive as quantified spiritual assessment (aqrab). Mouth-heart disconnect formula appears uniquely here. Battlefield context makes hypocrisy concrete rather than abstract.

candidates.label: Quadruple imperative closing: isbiruu/sabiroo/rabitoo/ittaqoo as comprehensive endurance formula for believers
candidates.definition: In 3:200: O you who have believed, be patient and endure and guard the frontiers and fear Allah that you may be successful.

evidence.excerpt: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱصۡبِرُواْ وَصَابِرُواْ وَرَابِطُواْ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
evidence.rationale: Four imperatives in sequence: isbiruu (be patient), sabiroo (endure/persevere), rabitoo (guard frontiers/bind together), ittaqoo Allah (fear Allah). La'allakum tuflihun provides success condition.

candidates.urduLabel: چار گنا حکم: صبر، ثبات، مرزبانی، تقویٰ
candidates.notes: Overlap with sabr-patience and patience-haste confirmed. Unique four-part imperative structure in Quran. Isbiruu vs sabiroo distinction suggests initial patience vs sustained endurance. Rabitoo adds communal/military dimension. Closes entire surah with actionable summary.

candidates.label: Blasphemous poverty claim: 'Allah is poor we are rich' as divinely recorded transgression warranting burning punishment
candidates.definition: In 3:181: Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is poor, while we are rich.' We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right and will say, 'Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.'

evidence.excerpt: لَّقَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٞ وَنَحۡنُ أَغۡنِيَآءُۘ سَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلَهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ
evidence.rationale: Laqad sami'a Allahu affirms divine hearing. Sanaktubu ma qaloo establishes permanent record. Dhooqoo adhab al-hareeq links speech to punishment.

candidates.urduLabel: کفریانہ دعویٰ: اللہ غریب ہم امیر
candidates.notes: Gap candidate: no dedicated blasphemy-types or divine-poverty-claim topic. Unique explicit quotation of anti-theological speech. Recording (sanaktubu) emphasizes accountability for speech. Paired with prophet-killing as dual transgression.

candidates.label: Steadfast prophetic precedent: rabbaniyyun and ahbar fighting alongside prophets without weakening or losing heart
candidates.definition: In 3:188: And how many a prophet fought alongside whom were many devoted scholars and followers. They did not lose heart for what afflicted them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. And Allah loves the steadfast.

evidence.excerpt: لَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفۡرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَواْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحۡمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمۡ يَفۡعَلُواْ فَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّهُم بِمَفَازَةٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡعَذَابِۖ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٞ
evidence.rationale: Ka-ayyin min nabiyyin qatala ma'ahu rabbaniyyoon kathir: quantitative emphasis. Ma wahanoo wa ma da'ufoo wa ma istakanoo: triple negation of weakness. Yuhibbu al-sabirin: divine love for steadfast.

candidates.urduLabel: ثابت قدم پیشروان: ربانیین اور احبار
candidates.notes: Overlap with sabr-patience confirmed. Variant of 3:146 ribbiyyun account with expanded vocabulary (rabbaniyyun + ahbar implied). Triple negation (wahan/da'f/istikanah) comprehensive resilience profile. Serves as historical encouragement for Uhud-weakened community.

candidates.label: Salvation formula: distance from Fire combined with Jannah admission as the definition of true success (fawz)
candidates.definition: In 3:185: So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained success.

evidence.excerpt: كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوۡنَ أُجُورَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۖ فَمَن زُحۡزِحَ عَنِ ٱلنَّارِ وَأُدۡخِلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ فَقَدۡ فَازَۗ وَمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡغُرُورِ
evidence.rationale: Fa-man zuhziha 'an al-nari wa udkhila al-jannata fa-qad faz: two-condition salvation formula. Zuhziha (drawn away/distance) implies active divine rescue. Faza defines ultimate success.

candidates.urduLabel: نجات کا فارمولا: آگ سے دوری اور جنت میں داخلہ
candidates.notes: Overlap with day-of-judgment confirmed. Most concise Quranic salvation formula. Two conditions necessary: negative (distance from Fire) AND positive (Jannah entry). Neither alone suffices. Faza vocabulary connects to falah (success) root.
